# 2323     "\n",
# 2324     "# # # #  🔍 What this code does:\n",
# 2325     "- The code groups log entries (`provider_log`) by their `called_by_type` (who invoked them) and `provider_type` (what kind of provider was called).\n",
# 2326     "- It then builds a flow network showing how control moves from one provider type to the next.\n",
# 2327     "- The width of each band represents the number of calls made along that path.\n",
# 2328     "\n",
# 2329     "# # # #  🧠 What you're seeing in the chart:\n",
# 2330     "- **Left-to-right flow** from high-level providers like `session`, `program`, and `controller`, down to mid-level like `system` and `state`, and finally to low-level workers like `agent`, `score`, and `tool`.\n",
# 2331     "- **Wider bands** indicate more frequent interactions. For example, the `state → score` and `score → tool` flows are thick, indicating heavy evaluation and tool usage.\n",
# 2332     "- **Branching paths** (e.g., from `agent` to `score`, `tool`, `agent_engine`) reveal the dependencies that agents rely on to make decisions.\n",

# 3186     "import plotly.graph_objects as go\n",
# 3187     "\n",
# 3188     "#  Prepare nodes and links\n",
# 3189     "df[\"source\"] = df[\"called_by_type\"].fillna(\"start\")\n",
# 3190     "df[\"target\"] = df[\"provider_type\"]\n",
# 3191     "\n",
# 3192     "nodes = list(set(df[\"source\"]) | set(df[\"target\"]))\n",
# 3193     "node_indices = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(nodes)}\n",
# 3194     "\n",
# 3195     "link_data = (\n",
# 3196     "    df.groupby([\"source\", \"target\"])\n",
# 3197     "    .size()\n",
# 3198     "    .reset_index(name=\"count\")\n",
# 3199     "    .assign(\n",
# 3200     "        source_idx=lambda d: d[\"source\"].map(node_indices),\n",
# 3201     "        target_idx=lambda d: d[\"target\"].map(node_indices)\n",
# 3202     "    )\n",
# 3203     ")\n",
# 3204     "\n",
# 3205     "fig = go.Figure(go.Sankey(\n",
# 3206     "    node=dict(\n",
# 3207     "        pad=15,\n",
# 3208     "        thickness=20,\n",
# 3209     "        line=dict(color=\"black\", width=0.5),\n",
# 3210     "        label=nodes\n",
# 3211     "    ),\n",
# 3212     "    link=dict(\n",
# 3213     "        source=link_data[\"source_idx\"],\n",
# 3214     "        target=link_data[\"target_idx\"],\n",
# 3215     "        value=link_data[\"count\"]\n",
# 3216     "    )\n",
# 3217     "))\n",
# 3218     "\n",

# 5042     "# # #  📦 Treemap of Provider Execution Cost\n",
# 5043     "\n",
# 5044     "This chart presents a **latency-weighted treemap** that reveals the **nested execution structure** of a CodeCritic run — from top-level orchestration down to fine-grained tooling.\n",
# 5045     "\n",
# 5046     "# # # #  🧠 What this code does:\n",
# 5047     "- **Builds a call hierarchy** by tracing each provider’s `called_by_type`, recursively reconstructing the execution path for every log entry.\n",
# 5048     "- **Flattens each path** into separate columns (e.g., `path_0`, `path_1`, ...) so Plotly can visualize the full call stack as a nested tree.\n",
# 5049     "- **Visualizes latency cost** using a treemap, where:\n",
# 5050     "  - Each **box** represents a provider type at a specific nesting level.\n",
# 5051     "  - **Box size** is proportional to total `latency_ms` contributed by that node and its descendants.\n",
# 5052     "  - **Color** corresponds to `provider_type`, using a colorblind-safe palette.\n",
# 5053     "\n",
# 5054     "# # # #  🔍 What you're observing:\n",
# 5055     "- The **upper-left boxes** show top-level orchestrators (e.g., `session`, `program`).\n",
# 5056     "- As you move inward (right and down), you see **nested calls** to `controller`, `system`, `state`, and ultimately `agent`, `tool`, `score`, etc.\n",
# 5057     "- **Larger boxes** deeper in the tree indicate subsystems that consume significant time (e.g., tools like `mypy`, `black`, `ruff`).\n",
# 5058     "- Hovering on a box reveals its exact path and latency.\n",
# 5059     "\n",
# 5060     "This visualization is ideal for:\n",
# 5061     "- Identifying where latency accumulates in multi-step workflows.\n",
# 5062     "- Spotting repeated or redundant calls.\n",

# 6401     "\n",
# 6402     "df[\"call_path\"] = df.apply(lambda row: build_path(row, edges), axis=1)\n",
# 6403     "\n",
# 6404     "#  Step 2: Flatten call path into real columns\n",
# 6405     "path_df = df[\"call_path\"].apply(pd.Series)\n",
# 6406     "path_df.columns = [f\"path_{i}\" for i in path_df.columns]\n",
# 6407     "\n",
# 6408     "#  Step 3: Combine into sunburst data source\n",
# 6409     "path_df = path_df.fillna(\"\")\n",
# 6410     "\n",
# 6411     "#  Then proceed as before\n",
# 6412     "sunburst_data = pd.concat([df, path_df], axis=1)\n",
# 6413     "\n",
# 6414     "\n",
# 6415     "fig = px.treemap(\n",
# 6416     "    sunburst_data,\n",
# 6417     "    path=path_df.columns.tolist(),\n",
# 6418     "    values=\"latency_ms\",\n",
# 6419     "    color=\"provider_type\",\n",
# 6420     "    color_discrete_sequence=px.colors.qualitative.Safe,\n",
# 6421     "    title=\"📦 Treemap of Provider Execution Cost\"\n",
# 6422     ")\n",
# 6423     "fig.show()\n"

# 6431     "# # #  🗺️ Provider Flow by Actor Type (One Node per Provider)\n",
# 6432     "\n",
# 6433     "This directed graph visualizes the **execution flow between unique providers** involved in a single run.\n",
# 6434     "\n",
# 6435     "# # # #  🧠 What this code does:\n",
# 6436     "- Extracts all log entries that include a `file_name`, sorted by time.\n",
# 6437     "- Groups logs by unique `(provider_type, provider_id)` pairs to ensure **each provider appears only once**.\n",
# 6438     "- Builds a directed graph showing **execution order** from one provider to the next.\n",
# 6439     "- Colors each node by `provider_type` (e.g. `system`, `state`, `agent`, `tool`) using a consistent palette.\n",
# 6440     "- Labels nodes as `<provider_type> (ID <provider_id>)`, making it easy to trace control flow.\n",
# 6441     "\n",
# 6442     "# # # #  🔍 What you're observing:\n",
# 6443     "- **Nodes** represent provider instances (e.g., `agent (ID 2)`, `tool (ID 1)`).\n",
# 6444     "- **Edges** represent transitions between providers during file processing, preserving execution order.\n",
# 6445     "- The layout is **stable** using a fixed seed, so it won't change between runs.\n",
# 6446     "- Helps reveal **which components are chained**, reused, or terminal in the flow.\n",
# 6447     "\n",
# 6448     "This visualization is especially useful for understanding how files propagate through an FSM-controlled execution graph, and for debugging orchestration logic.\n"
# 6449    ]

# 6469     "import networkx as nx\n",
# 6470     "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
# 6471     "\n",
# 6472     "#  Sort and dedupe by provider (only first appearance matters here)\n",
# 6473     "df_files = df[df[\"file_name\"].notna()].sort_values(\"timestamp\").copy()\n",
# 6474     "df_files = df_files[[\"timestamp\", \"provider_type\", \"provider_id\", \"file_name\"]].drop_duplicates()\n",
# 6475     "df_files[\"node\"] = df_files.apply(lambda row: f\"{row['provider_type']} (ID {row['provider_id']})\", axis=1)\n",
# 6476     "\n",
# 6477     "#  One row per provider node\n",
# 6478     "df_nodes = df_files.drop_duplicates(subset=[\"node\"]).reset_index(drop=True)\n",
# 6479     "\n",
# 6480     "#  Build node color mapping\n",
# 6481     "provider_types = df_nodes[\"provider_type\"].unique()\n",
# 6482     "color_map = dict(zip(provider_types, plt.get_cmap(\"tab10\").colors[:len(provider_types)]))\n",
# 6483     "node_colors = df_nodes[\"provider_type\"].map(color_map)\n",
# 6484     "\n",
# 6485     "#  Build edges between nodes (based on execution order)\n",
# 6486     "edges = []\n",
# 6487     "for i in range(1, len(df_nodes)):\n",
# 6488     "    prev = df_nodes.iloc[i - 1]\n",
# 6489     "    curr = df_nodes.iloc[i]\n",
# 6490     "    edges.append((prev[\"node\"], curr[\"node\"], curr[\"file_name\"]))\n",
# 6491     "\n",
# 6492     "#  Create graph\n",
# 6493     "G = nx.DiGraph()\n",
# 6494     "for src, tgt, label in edges:\n",
# 6495     "    G.add_edge(src, tgt, label=\"file\")\n",
# 6496     "\n",
# 6497     "#  Draw with color\n",
# 6498     "plt.figure(figsize=(14, 8))\n",
# 6499     "pos = nx.spring_layout(G, k=0.6, seed=32)  #  🔒 fixed layout\n",
# 6500     "\n",
# 6501     "nx.draw(\n",
# 6502     "    G, pos,\n",
# 6503     "    with_labels=True,\n",
# 6504     "    labels={node: node for node in G.nodes},\n",
# 6505     "    node_color=node_colors,\n",
# 6506     "    node_size=2000,\n",
# 6507     "    edge_color='gray',\n",
# 6508     "    arrows=True,\n",
# 6509     "    font_size=10\n",
# 6510     ")\n",
# 6511     "\n",
# 6512     "nx.draw_networkx_edge_labels(\n",
# 6513     "    G, pos,\n",
# 6514     "    edge_labels=nx.get_edge_attributes(G, 'label'),\n",
# 6515     "    font_size=8\n",
# 6516     ")\n",
# 6517     "\n",
# 6518     "plt.title(\"Provider Flow by Actor Type\", fontsize=14)  #  ⛔ no unsupported emoji\n",
# 6519     "plt.show()"
# 6520    ]

# 8835     "import plotly.express as px\n",
# 8836     "\n",
# 8837     "#  Sum latency by provider type\n",
# 8838     "latency_by_type = (\n",
# 8839     "    df.groupby(\"provider_type\")[\"latency_ms\"]\n",
# 8840     "    .sum()\n",
# 8841     "    .reset_index()\n",
# 8842     "    .sort_values(\"latency_ms\", ascending=False)\n",
# 8843     ")\n",
# 8844     "\n",
# 8845     "#  Plot as bar chart\n",
# 8846     "fig = px.bar(\n",
# 8847     "    latency_by_type,\n",
# 8848     "    x=\"provider_type\",\n",
# 8849     "    y=\"latency_ms\",\n",
# 8850     "    text=\"latency_ms\",\n",
# 8851     "    title=\"⏱️ Total Latency by Provider Type\",\n",
# 8852     "    labels={\"provider_type\": \"Provider Type\", \"latency_ms\": \"Total Latency (ms)\"},\n",
# 8853     "    color=\"provider_type\",\n",
# 8854     "    color_discrete_sequence=px.colors.qualitative.Pastel\n",
# 8855     ")\n",
# 8856     "fig.update_traces(textposition=\"outside\")\n",
# 8857     "fig.update_layout(xaxis_title=\"Provider Type\", yaxis_title=\"Total Latency (ms)\")\n",
# 8858     "fig.show()\n"
# 8859    ]
